newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called slightly higher on heat.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called slightly higher on heat.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open marginally higher again on Wednesday as stifling heat continued to prop up cash prices, sources said.
July over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.29 to $2.31 after settling to the upside Tuesday at $2.286 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, July wavered only slightly to last trade 0.2 cent lower at $2.284.
Early cash prices at Henry Hub were quoted at $2.31-2.34 per mmBtu.
Technical traders said resistance in July was at $2.36-2.37 and the contract high of $2.44. Support remained at the $2.151 double bottom, then at $2.13, $2.055 and $2.

In Tuesday's cash, Louisiana Gulf Coast prices firmed slightly to near $2.30. Midcon pipes gained a similar amount to the low-teens. New York city gate gas was quoted about five cents higher in the low-$2.60s.

Continuing to support cash were above-normal temperatures across the East, Midwest and Southwest, traders said. Cooler weather is forecast for Friday but a return of above-normal temperatures is expected this weekend.
Injection estimates for today's weekly AGA gas storage report range from 70 bcf to 100 bcf, versus a gain of 91 bcf a year ago.
